rules_text:
Rules summary Thanks to Mark Johnson (Eeeville) for his Tournay card descriptions used in the BGA adaptation! End game conditions The game ends when both of the following conditions are met, or if condition 1 is met by more than one player: A player has filled 9 spaces with at least 2 visible prestige buildings. One Town Crier card more than the number of players has been revealed. The last round is triggered at the beginning of the start player's turn, and each player gets a normal turn in this round. Then all players can choose a final card to play into their districts. Summary of turn actions Play a card from your hand (optional) Perform an action with citizen(s) (mandatory) Draw a card Activate a building in your district Combat an event Earn deniers Gather your citizens on your plaza Details of prestige buildings You cannot score more than 12 victory points from the same prestige building. If two players build the same prestige building there is only a single scoring. Yellow: Belfry : per set (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) of buildings or characters City Hall : per yellow citizen (2x) Cloth Hall : per yellow building or character (2x) Mint : per set of 4 deniers (2x) Tour des Six : per character (2x) White: Cathedral : only the player who builds it earns 8 PPs. La Madeleine : per prestige building (2x) Saint-Brice : per set (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) of buildings or characters Saint-Jacques : per white building or character (2x) Saint-Nicolas : per set of citizens you own (1 yellow +1 white +1 red) Saint-Quentin : per white citizen (2x) Red: Pont des Trous : per set (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) of citizens Porte de la Vigne : per red citizen (2x) Tour d’Arras : per white and yellow building (2x) Tour Henry VIII : per rampart built (2x) Tour Saint-Georges : per red card building or character (2x) Costs of citizens are payed by returning a citizen from your District, Plaza, or laying next to your Plaza, to the supply Costs of 1 card are payed by returning a Level I, II, or III card (i.e., not a Rampart) from your Hand or District (this is allowed to create a hole in your District) to its deck Prestige Building Colour # Cost to Play Builder Points Non-Builder Points Condition Belfry Yellow 1 5 deniers 4 2 each set of visible buildings or characters (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) City Hall Yellow 2 2 deniers, 1 card 2 1 each yellow citizen owned Cloth Hall Yellow 2 1 yellow citizen 2 1 each visible yellow building or character Mint Yellow 2 5 deniers 2 1 each set of 4 deniers Tour des Six Yellow 2 5 deniers 2 1 each visible character Cathedral White 1 20 deniers 8 0 none La Madeleine White 2 2 deniers, 1 card 2 1 each visible prestige building Saint-Brice White 1 5 deniers 4 2 each set of visible buildings or characters (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) Saint-Jacques White 2 1 white citizen 2 1 each visible white building or character Saint-Nicolas White 1 5 deniers 3 1 each set of citizens you own (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) Saint-Quentin White 2 2 deniers, 1 card 2 1 each white citizen owned Pont des Trous Red 1 5 deniers 3 1 each set of citizens you own (1 yellow + 1 white + 1 red) Porte de la Vigne Red 2 2 deniers, 1 card 2 1 each red citizen owned Tour d’Arras Red 2 5 deniers 2 1 each visible white and yellow building Tour Henry VIII Red 2 5 deniers 2 1 each rampart card built Tour Saint-Georges Red 2 1 red citizen 2 1 each visible red building or character

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] This game was absolutely horrid.   Absolutely no decision making of interest at all. Couldn't finish the second game. Sorely disappointed.

[Rating: 1/10] Won my first three games of this without knowing exactly what I was doing and had no idea why or how I came out on top. That's partially my fault for not having a better understanding of the game, but the fact that I won not once, not twice, but thrice, against people that had played the game previously, does not bode well for the game itself. Found it mostly boring and often felt at the mercy of random card draws. I much prefer the dice mitigation and manipulation of TROYES.

[Rating: 2/10] The rulebook is just terrible which makes this infuriating to play. Look at RftG to see how icons should be used and explained. Rating may change if someone explained the rules, but I'd just prefer to play a different game.

[Rating: 2/10] Frustrating, limited options, often there's nothing interesting to do, almost always actions are sooo limited, lots of luck. Single play, hated it after 4 rounds, maybe I'm missing something but can't see what.

[Rating: 2.5/10] On a coupé la game au milieu car c'était plus long que prévu. Une iconographie dégueu, pas de rappel de toutes les cartes. FAQ indispensable.  Charte graphique de Troyes dégueu.  Le jeu outre ces très graves défauts avait pas l'air top ...

[Rating: 3/10] Quirky mechanics take some time to learn.  Conveys no sense of the history of the city, and I found little strategic depth.
